content:
ops-bot: INCIDENT detected: embeddings route (embed.v1) token service CPU spike + increased 5xxs. Paging on-call: @james-oncall

james-oncall: on it. digging into alerts. which routes impacted most? any customer-facing errors? :eyes:

maria-sre: p95 token latency for embed.v1 spiked 4x since 09:12 UTC, error rate from 0.2% -> 3.8%. heavy tail looks like a small set of large batched requests and some rerank calls hitting the same pool.

leo-api: confirmed: rerank-route (rerank.v2) and embeddings-public (embed.v1.public) both hit the same GPU pool due to recent routing change. rerank has bigger KV/cache churn.

james-oncall: priority: prevent cascade to other tenants. propose temporary per-endpoint quota tweak: reduce embeddings-public concurrency and lower rerank throughput to low-priority pool. also consider disabling on-the-fly similarity scoring flag for non-enterprise orgs. agree?

devon-eng: +1. we can apply a targeted quota change via Admin API. quick patch: reduce embed.v1.public qps from 3000 -> 800, rerank.v2 from 1200 -> 400 and set rerank to route_priority=low for new traffic. will prepare command.

devon-eng: ```bash
# admin API (dry-run) - apply per-endpoint quota
curl -X POST https://admin.redwood.internal/v1/quotas/update \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${ADMIN_TOKEN}" \
  -d '{"changes": [{"route":"embed.v1.public","qps":800},{"route":"rerank.v2","qps":400,"priority":"low"}]}'
```

carla-cs: pulling impacted orgs list now. I need to inform any affected paying customers proactively if we disable similarity scoring. ETA 10m.

maria-sre: note: embeddings-heavy customer (org-842) is doing very large multi-file batches; recommend we whitelist enterprise-critical orgs or reduce their batch size via per-org cap rather than global throttle.

james-oncall: good call. plan: 1) apply per-endpoint quota tweaks (targeted) 2) apply per-org batch size cap for org-842 (temporary) 3) move rerank traffic to low-priority pool 4) notify CS/SEs. fallback: rollback quotas and re-enable features if latency normalizes.

devon-eng: applying step 1 now (will do canary on 2 nodes):

infra-bot: RUNNING: quota-update-job 1755555567 by devon-eng

infra-bot: CANARY COMPLETE: 2/2 nodes applied, no immediate errors (1755555574)

infra-bot: APPLIED: embed.v1.public qps=800, rerank.v2 qps=400, rerank priority set to low (1755555576)

maria-sre: seeing p95 drop to 1.6x within 30s of canary, 5xxs down to 1.1%. good signal. continuing roll out across pool.

devon-eng: applying per-org cap for org-842: batch_size_max=50 (was 500). command posted to runbook.

infra-bot: APPLIED: org cap org-842 batch_size_max=50 (1755555582)

carla-cs: notified contacts for org-842 and told them we may ask to throttle large jobs; they acknowledged, will coordinate. added to incident email.

leo-api: re-route complete: rerank load now served from low-priority pool, evictions expected but no client errors so far. will monitor queue lengths.

james-oncall: monitoring dashboard: token CPU usage trending down, error rates falling. recommend keep caps for 30m then re-evaluate. leaving rerank at low priority for 1h.

maria-sre: adding note to incident timeline: root cause likely routing change coupled with a large batched job. follow-ups: autoscaling tuning for rerank pool, stricter per-org batch sizing, and add alert for correlated route spikes.

carla-cs: drafting customer comms for affected customers, will send once we confirm stabilization.

james-oncall: engaging postmortem owners: @devon-eng (mitigations), @maria-sre (root cause + alerts), @leo-api (routing rollback plan).

infra-bot: STATUS: mitigation applied, metrics improving. Incident severity reduced to SEV3.

james-oncall: thanks team. if metrics stable for 30m we close. leaving this thread open for updates. :white_check_mark:
